comment: Unfiltered polarizing exposure set; GCN 22444 reports the telescope was pointed at 2018-02-24 22:21:44 UT, +37 s from the Swift trigger, and gives a maximum magnitude of approximately 16.7. The same set had an approximately 5σ limiting magnitude of 18.1; this is not a separate nondetection row. Exposure duration and exact midpoint are not reported, so the stated pointing time is used as the time anchor and time_err is left blank.

Swift/UVOT 3σ measurement from GCN 22454; stated T_start=61 s, T_stop=211 s, Exp=294 s. Time and time_err use the midpoint and half-width of the published T_start/T_stop interval; magnitudes are in the UVOT system (Vega) and are not corrected for Galactic extinction (E(B−V)=0.01). GCN 22442 reports the overlapping early White finding-chart result 18.94±0.15 at +160 s (150 s exposure); it may be the same early data product, but the overlapping windows and different exposure totals prevent confirming identity, so both records are retained. GCN 22454 lists 294 s exposure across a 150 s T_start/T_stop span; the published window is used for timing and this mismatch is preserved.

Swift/UVOT White finding-chart exposure: GCN 22442 says it started +85 s after BAT T0 and lasted 150 s; time is the midpoint +160 s and time_err is half the exposure. GCN 22442 does not state a magnitude system, so mag_system remains blank.

Unfiltered polarizing first exposure set; GCN 22444 gives UT=2018-02-24 22:24:12, +185 s from Swift T0=22:21:07. The circular also says 176 s after trigger (about 8.3 s difference using precise BAT trigger 22:21:07.7253). It only says the telescope was pointed and gives a first-set 5σ limit of about 15.8 mag; exposure duration and start/stop are absent, so the absolute UT pointing time is the only usable anchor and the exposure midpoint cannot be recovered. time_err remains blank.

OA-SDG 0.5m Rc upper limit from GCN 22452. The circular gives start=2018-02-24 23:33:36 UT, 9×180 s, and R>20.2; using the absolute start and half of the 1620 s total exposure gives midpoint 23:47:06 UT (time=+5159 s from the integer Swift T0=22:21:07 UT; MJD retained from this midpoint). The circular’s “about 1.21 hours after the trigger” is approximate and does not match the precise absolute time, so the absolute UT and exposure sequence anchor the record. The previous time=5122 s was measured from the erroneous old T0=22:21:44 UT.

RATIR r/i photometry from GCN 22446; source gives the observing window 2018/02/25.23–.53 UT (midpoint .38 UT), equivalent to T+7.24–14.42 h, and 3.91 h total exposure. Time uses the midpoint of the stated UT window, time_err is half the 0.30 d window; magnitudes are AB and uncorrected for Galactic extinction.
